[Textbook misprint: the book prints \(\dfrac{117}{3}-\dfrac{21}{2}=\dfrac{234-83}{6}\), but \(\dfrac{21}{2}=\dfrac{63}{6}\), so the numerator is \(234-63\). It then prints the answer as \(\dfrac{151}{3}\), which is neither \(\dfrac{151}{6}\) nor the true value. The integral equals \(\dfrac{171}{6}=\dfrac{57}{2}\).]

\(\int_{2}^{5}(x^{2} - x)\,dx = \left[\left(\dfrac{x^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right)\right]_{2}^{5}\)
\(= \left[\left(\dfrac{5^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{5^{2}}{2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{2^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{2^{2}}{2}\right)\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{125}{3} - \dfrac{25}{2} - \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{4}{2}\)
\(= \dfrac{117}{3} - \dfrac{21}{2} = \dfrac{234 - 83}{6}\)
\(\therefore \int_{2}^{5}(x^{2} - x)\,dx = \dfrac{151}{3}\)

\(I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\sin^{2} x\,dx\) ... (i)
\(= \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{3} - x\right)dx\)
\(= \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\sin^{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\right)dx\)
\(I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\cos^{2} x\,dx\) ... (ii)
adding (i) and (ii)
\(2I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\sin^{2} x\,dx + \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\cos^{2} x\,dx\)
\(2I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}(\sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x)\,dx\)
\(2I = \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3} 1\,dx = \left[x\right]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\)
\(2I = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\)  \(\therefore I = \dfrac{\pi}{12}\)
\(\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\sin^{2} x\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{12}\)

[Textbook misprint: the opening line reads "Let \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log(1+\tan x)\,dx\) ... (i)" with no \(I=\), although every later line, and the reference "by eq. (i)", depend on \(I\) having been named there. Restored as \(I=\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log(1+\tan x)\,dx\). The answer \(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\log 2\) is correct.]

Let \(\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log(1 + \tan x)\,dx\) ... (i)
\(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log\left[1 + \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - x\right)\right]dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log\left[1 + \dfrac{\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \tan x}{1 + \tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\cdot\tan x}\right]dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log\left[1 + \dfrac{1 - \tan x}{1 + \tan x}\right]dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log\left[\dfrac{1 + \tan x + 1 - \tan x}{1 + \tan x}\right]dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log\left[\dfrac{2}{1 + \tan x}\right]dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\left[\log 2 - \log(1 + \tan x)\right]dx\)
\(= \int_{0}^{\pi/4}(\log 2)\,dx - \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log(1 + \tan x)\,dx\)
\(I = (\log 2)\int_{0}^{\pi/4} 1\,dx - I\) ... by eq. (i)
\(I + I = (\log 2)\left[x\right]_{0}^{\pi/4}\)
\(2I = (\log 2)\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4} - 0\right]\)
\(\therefore I = \dfrac{\pi}{8}(\log 2)\)
Thus
\(\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\log(1 + \tan x)\,dx = \dfrac{\pi}{8}(\log 2)\)

Let \(f(x) = x^{3}\sin^{4} x\)
\(f(-x) = (-x)^{3}\left[\sin(-x)\right]^{4} = -x^{3}\left[-\sin x\right]^{4} = -x^{3}\sin^{4} x\)
\(= -f(x)\)
\(f(x)\) is odd function.
\(\therefore \int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4} x^{3}\sin^{4} x\,dx = 0\)

[Textbook misprint: the book prints \(2\{(1-\tan^{-1}x)-(0-\tan^{-1}x)\}\), substituting the limits into \(x\) but not into \(\tan^{-1}x\); as printed the two \(\tan^{-1}x\) terms simply cancel. It should read \(2\{(1-\tan^{-1}1)-(0-\tan^{-1}0)\}\). The answer \(\dfrac{4-\pi}{2}\) is correct.]

Let \(f(x) = \dfrac{x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}\)
\(f(-x) = \dfrac{(-x)^{2}}{1 + (-x)^{2}}\)
\(= \dfrac{x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}\)
\(= f(x)\)
\(f(x)\) is even function.
\(\int_{-1}^{1}\dfrac{x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}\,dx\)
\(= 2\int_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1 + x^{2} - 1}{1 + x^{2}}\,dx\)
\(= 2\int_{0}^{1}\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + x^{2}}\right]dx\)
\(= 2\left[x - \tan^{-1} x\right]_{0}^{1}\)
\(= 2\left\{(1 - \tan^{-1} x) - (0 - \tan^{-1} x)\right\}\)
\(= 2\left\{1 - \dfrac{\pi}{4} - 0\right\}\)
\(= 2\left(1 - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \left(\dfrac{4 - \pi}{2}\right)\)
\(\therefore \int_{-1}^{1}\dfrac{x^{2}}{1 + x^{2}}\,dx = \dfrac{4 - \pi}{2}\)
